key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage concentrated near the buried hole-transport-layer interface in p-i-n perovskite solar cells.
engineering_relevance: This approach enables rapid interface-stability screening, while 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification reduces buried-interface damage and improves UV stability.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe different depths.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL, and ideality-factor measurements.
Compare perovskite films and devices with different ITO modifiers during UV soaking.
evidence_signal: Nondestructive measurements identify preferential degradation at the hole-transport-layer interface, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests, and show improved UV stability with interface modification.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative stability gains or depth resolution, and UV-soaking results alone do not establish long-term operational durability.
paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
